before: bufio.Scanner splits input into tokens; its default split is lines with line endings removed. Scanner has a maximum token size, so it is not an unlimited line reader. Buffer configures the starting buffer and maximum before scanning starts.

Scan returning false can mean end-of-input or a failure. Always inspect Err after the loop. This fixture chooses a tiny maximum of eight bytes and prints a stable label rather than depending on the exact error text. A larger configured limit still needs an application size policy.
Expected output or behavior: 1. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Choose a justified production limit and explain when a Reader may be more appropriate than Scanner. You may trace it without a Go compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A Scanner reads input in pieces called tokens. By default, each token is one line without its line ending. Scanner has a size limit. Set its buffer before scanning; this example sets a small maximum of eight bytes.
`Scan()` returns false when input ends or when a problem stops scanning. After the loop, `Err()` tells these cases apart. A nil error means no scanning failure was reported.
The screen shows `1`. The short line fits, so the loop counts one line and finishes without an error.
A line of twenty plain letters is too large for this tiny limit. Choose a limit that fits the task; use a different reading approach when lines may be much larger.

before.question: If the input is a twenty-character line, what happens under this configured limit?
choices: The scanner silently accepts unlimited lines.
Scan false can only mean a clean EOF.
The scanner reports an error; the program prints scan failed.
before.explanation: The token exceeds the small configured maximum, and Err distinguishes that failure from normal exhaustion.

after.question: What happens with a line of twenty plain letters?
choices: The scanner accepts lines of any size.
Scan returning false always means a clean end.
The scanner reports an error, and the program shows scan failed.
after.explanation: The line exceeds the configured limit. Err reports the problem after Scan stops.
